Determine a set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ that generate the above parabola. Express your answer in the form $x=2pt,y=p{t}^{2},$ where $p$ is a constant.

$x=$
{{field-1}},
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(10,5).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(10,5),$ we can substitute $x=10$ and $y=5$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}10=2pt \\ 5=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & =2pt \\ 5 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{5}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =p{(\frac{5}{p})}^{2} \\ 5 & =p\cdot \frac{25}{{p}^{2}} \\ 5 & =\frac{25}{p} \\ p & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(5)t,\,y=(5){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=10t,\,y=5{t}^{2}.
$$
